about: The shipped panel table's numbers (apps/quest-tracker/crates/qt-screen/src/panel_table.rs): per probe, what `quest-tracker-replay panels measure` printed for it and the limits set from those numbers; then the probe statistics of sampled frames, as `quest-tracker-replay panels probe --frame` prints them with the shipped table. Numbers, times and ids only: no pixel, crop, frame or OCR text. The tests paint synthetic copies from these numbers.
frames: Every number here comes from quality-90 JPEG frames, written through GDI+ by tools/quest_tracker/outside/capture.ps1 (whole client rect, 2560x1440) and decoded by qt-capture. The watcher reads raw GDI copies, so the limits keep the margin rules for raw copies.

sessions.live-1: The no-kill footprint session (the research note's Live 12), 2026-10-27, a town, 4 frames a second; the table was chosen on it. Windows from its panels.txt, presses as kept.
sessions.live-8: The research note's Live 8, 2026-10-26, another character in The Riverbank, 2 frames a second; the hold-out the table was not tuned on.

rules.footprint: the panel's own extent as its frames show it, looked at locally; never measure's footprint, which is the whole client for every Live 1 panel (background and HUD changes)
rules.black: a read is black only when every probe's copy is black; a black copy among others simply does not match
rules.grid: measure's 160 x 90 grid of the client rect; a probe is one patch, cell (col, row)
rules.tolerance: per channel, the larger of 3 x spread and 6 levels, capped at margin / 2; a probe squeezed below 6 is dropped
rules.max_luma_std: the larger of 2 x luma_std + 8 and 16 when least is above the largest tolerance (every probe here); otherwise 2 x luma_std + 4
rules.not_dark: the probe's centre luma less its largest tolerance is at least 16
rules.factors_are: this workorder's choice, not a measurement

unlabelled.what: the inventory open before its press
the inventory, with the stash, open before its press
the inventory open before its press

samples_are: open: frames of a window's detected run (Live 1 from its first frame, Live 8 with an opening run of misses left out; never a frame of a closing run of misses), only the entry standing for that window's panel; closed: Live 1 frames outside every window's margins (3 s before, 2 s after) and outside the unlabelled stretches, Live 1's character-panel windows, and Live 8's foreground play-span frames outside every window's margins, every entry; Live 1's and Live 8's Escape-menu windows (frames the measured, not shipped Escape-menu entry reads open, the game in the foreground), every entry, since the Escape menu hides nothing. Closed samples recorded before that choice also carry that entry's probes and read

entries.chosen: the inventory's header plate (rows 10 to 22, columns 120 to 141); the stash's and a merchant's windows open the inventory beside them, so they share this entry; (141, 10) is never black in a closed frame of either session, so a dark scene cannot make the whole read black

the title plate (row 2), the only candidates that also find Live 8's tree (another character); (145, 12) on the frame's right is never black in a closed frame, so a dark scene cannot make the whole read black

the microtransactions shop (the owner's name for M); flat patches on its left column, and (140, 9) and (150, 8) on its top right, never black in a closed frame, so a dark scene behind the closed shop cannot make the whole read black
the options (the owner's name for O), a panel on the left: its header (row 5) and two patches of its foot
the world map (the owner's name for U): its title plate (row 2) and two patches of its frame (row 24)

not_shipped.chosen: the top of the menu box (rows 25 to 32, columns 71 to 84), static art the same in both sessions
not_shipped.why: measured in Live 1 and kept as data, not shipped: the owner chose on 2026-10-27, during Live 2 (which had measured it hiding the overlay), that the overlay stays shown while the Escape menu is open; the closed samples hold Escape-menu frames that every shipped entry reads closed
